definition.label: Begging the question
definition.definition: Assuming, directly or indirectly, the very point that needs to be established, so the conclusion is smuggled into the premises.

source.sectionTitle: Consciousness as primitive and the explanation of matter
source.currentDescription: Because consciousness conditions every possible comparison, McGilchrist concludes it cannot be conventionally defined and must instead serve as experience’s irreducible ontological ground.
source.lockedProposition: Consciousness cannot be defined by comparison because it is the ground within which every comparison and experience occurs.
source.completeLockedSourceExcerpt: I think the first thing to say is that it's difficult to specify what consciousness is because it's just the ground of everything, and therefore there is nothing with which one could conceivably compare it.
source.assessmentRationale: Strongest feature: McGilchrist carefully turns the definitional difficulty into a coherent foundational claim: comparison presupposes consciousness, so consciousness cannot straightforwardly be specified through something experientially external to it. Principal limitation: The phenomenological observation does not independently establish that consciousness is literally “the ground of everything,” and it supplies almost no comparative reason to prefer participatory co-creation over Kastrup’s equally consciousness-first idealism. Live burden: He still must connect primitive consciousness to relational encounter, explain why universality entails ontological fundamentality rather than merely epistemic indispensability, and demonstrate an advantage unavailable to the agreed rival framework.

presentedReviews.rationale: Calling consciousness the ground of everything is insufficiently established, but the move offers a comparison-based reason rather than simply restating its conclusion as a premise.

Calling consciousness the ground of everything is a contested foundational premise, but the move offers comparison's dependence on consciousness as a reason; it does not circularly derive that premise from itself.

definition.label: Argument from ignorance
definition.definition: Treating a claim as true because it has not been disproved, or false because it has not been proved, rather than supplying positive evidence.

source.sectionTitle: Consciousness as primitive and the explanation of matter
source.currentDescription: McGilchrist replies that matter manifests consciousness and is knowable only as an element within consciousness, while acknowledging substantial proximity to Kastrup’s representational proposal.
source.lockedProposition: Matter is a way consciousness manifests, and matter is known to us only as an element within consciousness that we designate material.
source.completeLockedSourceExcerpt: But my view on matter is that it is a way in which consciousness can manifest. And that may be similar to what actually Bernadette was saying, but in other words, that it is. I mean, the first thing to say is that, we we only know about matter because it is an element in consciousness that we choose to call material.
source.assessmentRationale: Strongest feature: McGilchrist commendably acknowledges substantial agreement and offers manifestation as a consciousness-first alternative, avoiding any suggestion that matter exists independently of experience or opposes mentality. Principal limitation: The fact that matter is known only within consciousness establishes an epistemic condition, not the ontological conclusion that matter is consciousness manifesting, while “manifestation,” “phase,” and “element” remain insufficiently differentiated. Live burden: He must articulate a mechanism distinguishing manifestation from representation and show why that distinction improves explanation of resistance, perception, or participation.

presentedReviews.rationale: The move improperly advances from an epistemic condition to an ontological proposal, but it does not claim manifestation is true merely because an alternative remains unproved.

And that may be similar to what actually Bernadette was saying, but in other words, that it is. presentedReviews.rationale: The move inadequately crosses from matter being known in consciousness to matter being consciousness manifest, but this is an unsupported epistemic-to-ontological inference rather than a premise that restates its conclusion.

definition.label: Red herring
definition.definition: Diverting attention from the issue under dispute to a related but less relevant point, leaving the original challenge insufficiently answered.

source.sectionTitle: Representation, perception, and access to reality
source.currentDescription: Against a merely representational description, McGilchrist argues that right-hemisphere attention actively brings the encountered phenomenon into presence rather than registering something passively given.
source.lockedProposition: For right-hemisphere awareness, what is attended to is not merely passively present but comes into presence through attention.
source.completeLockedSourceExcerpt: A very important distinction I make between the way a right hemisphere works and the left hemisphere works is a right hemisphere is where whatever it is that we are attending to or aware of presence is to use that high tech area and term. But I mean, you can't say is present, but it presence is means not just that it's sort of passively sitting there, but it comes about for you through that attention.
source.assessmentRationale: Strongest feature: McGilchrist introduces an important participatory intuition: attention is not neutral reception but helps determine how an encountered reality becomes present to a conscious subject. Principal limitation: The hemispheric premise is unsupported within the move, “presence” lacks operational definition, and Kastrup’s active encoding process need not portray perception as passively registering an already finished object. Live burden: McGilchrist must demonstrate that attentive constitution is incompatible with, or explanatorily superior to, perspectival encoding rather than simply describing a complementary aspect of perception.

presentedReviews.rationale: The contrast with passive presence inadequately engages Kastrup's active encoding account, but attention and perceptual presentation remain directly relevant to the disputed issue rather than a diversion from it.

definition.label: Base-rate neglect
definition.definition: Underweighting general background rates or prior probabilities while focusing too heavily on a vivid specific case or local detail.

source.sectionTitle: Representation, perception, and access to reality
source.currentDescription: McGilchrist answers that perception normally constructs reality dependably, while specially confusing conditions can exploit the visual system and produce genuine but incorrect experiences.
source.lockedProposition: The brain ordinarily puts reality together successfully, but deliberately confusing conditions can make the visual system produce an incorrect experience.
source.completeLockedSourceExcerpt: but generally speaking, are we are the victims of the skill with which our brain helps to put together reality. At 99.99% or more of the time, it does a very, very good job. But if you deliberately set out to make it confusing for the optical system, then you will see something that is not correct.
source.assessmentRationale: Strongest feature: McGilchrist directly reconciles authentic perceptual contact with error by presenting the brain as a normally successful but fallible interpreter rather than a transparent or infallible window. Principal limitation: The “99.99%” reliability estimate is unsupported, and treating illusions as exceptional engineered confusion understates naturally occurring and structurally systematic divergences between experienced qualities and stimuli. Live burden: He must explain why constructive neural interpretation still constitutes direct participatory contact and provide a principled boundary separating ordinary disclosure from representational mediation.

presentedReviews.rationale: The unsupported 99.99% estimate and understatement of naturally occurring illusions weaken the claim, but no supplied background rate is underweighted in favor of a vivid local case.

definition.label: Red herring
definition.definition: Diverting attention from the issue under dispute to a related but less relevant point, leaving the original challenge insufficiently answered.

source.sectionTitle: Representation, perception, and access to reality
source.currentDescription: Kastrup contends that literal perceptual mirroring would permit unbounded internal entropy and potentially fatal perception, so bounded organisms require mediated rather than transparent worldly access.
source.lockedProposition: If perceptual states mirrored unrestricted worldly states, internal entropy would lose its upper bound and perception itself could become fatal.
source.completeLockedSourceExcerpt: So the argument goes that if our perceptual states, which are in us would mirror the states of the world, that's, that's the only way we could see. We see the world as it is. It's for our internal perceptual percept, perceptual states to mirror the states of the world. If they did that, then we would not have an upper bound in our internal and internal entropy, and we could die just by perceiving.
source.assessmentRationale: Strongest feature: Kastrup attempts to move beyond isolated illusions by offering a structural reason that biologically bounded perceivers require selective encoding rather than unrestricted correspondence with external states. Principal limitation: The crucial bridge from perceptual mirroring to unbounded internal entropy is neither defined nor defended, and the argument reconstructs McGilchrist’s qualified encounter as stronger literal state replication. Live burden: Kastrup must specify the relevant entropy, demonstrate why informational covariance threatens organismic integrity, and show that participatory contact entails the prohibited mirroring relation.

presentedReviews.rationale: The entropy objection substitutes unrestricted internal mirroring for McGilchrist's expressly qualified contact claim, so it attacks a related stronger thesis while leaving the actual position unanswered.
presentedReviews.context: if our perceptual states, which are in us would mirror the states of the world

definition.label: Begging the question
definition.definition: Assuming, directly or indirectly, the very point that needs to be established, so the conclusion is smuggled into the premises.

source.sectionTitle: Field, relation, participation, and subject boundaries
source.currentDescription: Kastrup argues that genuine reality must exist experientially for itself, concluding that the world’s intrinsic qualities—not merely another observer’s representation—constitute what it is.
source.lockedProposition: Anything that truly exists must exist for itself rather than only as another mind's representation; therefore the world's own experiential qualities are what it really is.
source.completeLockedSourceExcerpt: everything that really exists must exist for itself. In other words, it cannot be limited to a representation in some other mind. It must feel like something to itself. So, the world exists to itself. Meaning there is something it is like to be it. There are certain qualities associated with being the world. And the argument would be that those qualities are what the world really is, what it is like to be the world is what the world really is.
source.assessmentRationale: Strongest feature: Kastrup clearly distinguishes the world’s intrinsic subjectivity from any localized observer’s representation, thereby preventing analytic idealism from collapsing reality into appearances inside personal minds. Principal limitation: The universal premise that everything real must feel like something to itself is asserted rather than independently defended, and it does not establish that nature forms one unified subject instead of many experiential centers. Live burden: Kastrup must warrant intrinsic subjectivity, explain unity and dissociation, and show why the world’s own qualities are epistemically accessible enough to support the proposed comparison.

presentedReviews.rationale: The universal premise that everything real must feel like something to itself already assumes the intrinsic subjectivity needed to conclude that the world experiences itself.
presentedReviews.context: everything that really exists must exist for itself. It must feel like something to itself.

presentedReviews.rationale: The universal claim that everything real exists and feels for itself is asserted without adequate defense, but a contested or unsupported premise alone does not establish circular reasoning under the supplied definition.

definition.label: Appeal to authority
definition.definition: Relying on a person or institution's status as if it settles the argument, especially when the relevant evidence, expertise, or consensus has not been shown.

source.sectionTitle: Constraint, agency, freedom, and novelty
source.currentDescription: If divine creation is genuinely relational love, McGilchrist argues, communion requires a free other, making novelty and developing relationship preferable to fixed exhaustive divine completion.
source.lockedProposition: If God's relation to creation is creative love, communion with the created other requires that other to have freedom.
source.completeLockedSourceExcerpt: which is that the nature of God in all religions. I know of is something relational, and the nature of that relation is usually said to be creative love. Now, if it is creative love, it is to bring something about. And it is experience. Love. The other that it must be in come in communion with must have freedom.
source.assessmentRationale: Strongest feature: McGilchrist develops a powerful conditional chain from creative love through genuine otherness to freedom, directly connecting divine relation with novelty instead of treating creation as predetermined display. Principal limitation: The broad religious generalization is unsupported, relational love does not automatically establish libertarian freedom, and Kastrup’s qualified omniscience need not imply exhaustive foreknowledge or erase otherness. Live burden: McGilchrist must specify the freedom required, demonstrate its compatibility with divine inclusion, and answer Kastrup’s possibility that mind-at-large genuinely discovers an irreducible future.

presentedReviews.rationale: The unsupported generalization about religions is evidence-poor, but the speaker does not invoke any religion's prestige or expertise as independently settling the argument about divine relation.

The reference to religions is a broad empirical generalization about conceptions of God, not reliance on religious authorities' status as though that status settled the inference from love to freedom.

definition.label: Appeal to authority
definition.definition: Relying on a person or institution's status as if it settles the argument, especially when the relevant evidence, expertise, or consensus has not been shown.

source.sectionTitle: Constraint, agency, freedom, and novelty
source.currentDescription: Because selection favors adaptive behavior rather than intrinsic-world accuracy, Kastrup argues that evolved perception should encode fitness-relevant appearances that can diverge from reality’s own experiential qualities.
source.lockedProposition: Evolution optimizes perception for fitness rather than faithful mirroring, so adaptive presentation should diverge from the world's intrinsic states.
source.completeLockedSourceExcerpt: the non Hofmann's argument, which is based on game theory, which is that evolution would never optimize for us to perceive the world as it is. It would optimize for us to see the world in whatever way it would be more conducive to fitness. And then he ran all these experiments, mathematical experiments, to show that, in fact, that these two things would tend to depart,
source.assessmentRationale: Strongest feature: Kastrup supplies a recognizable evolutionary mechanism for selective presentation, explaining why a localized organism might receive action-guiding appearances rather than an exhaustive disclosure of intrinsic reality. Principal limitation: The categorical claim that evolution would “never” optimize veridical perception overstates the summarized modeling, since fitness and accuracy can correlate and the underlying game-theoretic assumptions are not presented. Live burden: He must establish the degree and character of predicted divergence, connect adaptive encoding to analytic idealism specifically, and answer McGilchrist’s possibility of partial but genuine contact.

presentedReviews.rationale: Hoffman's work is cited and summarized as a game-theoretic argument, not treated as true solely because of Hoffman's status; the defect is overstatement and omitted assumptions.

Kastrup names Hoffman's game-theoretic work but also states its evolutionary rationale and reported modeling result; the defect identified is categorical overstatement, not substituting Hoffman's status for evidence.

definition.label: Appeal to authority
definition.definition: Relying on a person or institution's status as if it settles the argument, especially when the relevant evidence, expertise, or consensus has not been shown.

source.sectionTitle: God, mind-at-large, and cosmic intelligence
source.currentDescription: A single cell’s apparently novel response to an unprecedented threat exemplifies intelligence for McGilchrist, supporting creative responsiveness throughout nature rather than intelligence as mere complexity.
source.lockedProposition: A single cell's novel, unprogrammed response to a threat exemplifies intelligence as adaptive handling of an unprepared situation.
source.completeLockedSourceExcerpt: She also thought that a single cell could mobilize an intelligent response to a threat that it had never experienced before, and that it wasn't prepared by any set of instructions on how to do it. So to me, that is really, what intelligence is.
source.assessmentRationale: Strongest feature: McGilchrist proposes a functional marker of intelligence—adaptive response to an unprepared situation—that is more discriminating and purpose-relevant than sheer structural vastness or complexity. Principal limitation: The cellular example depends on an unnamed authority, and the claim that no inherited, biochemical, or environmentally prepared instructions explain the response is not demonstrated within the move. Live burden: McGilchrist must document the behavior, define “unprogrammed” biologically, and connect local cellular adaptability to cosmic intelligence and value-directed participatory purpose.

presentedReviews.rationale: The cellular example depends on an unnamed source and lacks documentation, but no identifiable person's authority or institutional standing is offered as what settles the conclusion.

The cellular example depends on an unnamed researcher's report and lacks supporting detail, but citation or evidentiary dependence alone does not show reliance on that person's authority as dispositive.

definition.label: Scope neglect
definition.definition: Failing to adjust judgment in proportion to the scale, number, or magnitude of what is being discussed.

source.sectionTitle: God, mind-at-large, and cosmic intelligence
source.currentDescription: Given that physical structure represents mental states, Kastrup infers from the cosmos’s immense complexity a correspondingly vast intelligence exceeding anything humans can explicitly conceptualize.
source.lockedProposition: If the physical cosmos represents mental states, its vast structured complexity suggests an intelligence beyond explicit human conception.
source.completeLockedSourceExcerpt: If the universe, the physical universe, the inanimate universe out there, such as analytic idealism would say is just a representation of mental states, then the sheer vastness and complexity of, you know, the web of galaxies would suggest that it's any vast intelligence incommensurable with anything we could explicitly conceive in our own mind.
source.assessmentRationale: Strongest feature: Kastrup connects the representational premise to cosmic scale in an intelligible conditional: immensely structured appearances would correspond to mental activity vastly exceeding localized human conception. Principal limitation: Complexity alone does not entail intelligence, and the move compares no non-intelligent source of structured order; moreover, representation by itself cannot establish the purposive or adaptive character usually associated with intelligence. Live burden: Kastrup must define intelligence independently of magnitude, show why galactic complexity supports that criterion, and distinguish his inference from McGilchrist’s responsiveness-based conception.

presentedReviews.rationale: The move gives cosmic vastness and complexity too much evidential weight, but it does not ignore or fail to scale judgment with magnitude; magnitude is expressly emphasized, so the exact bias is absent.

definition.label: Begging the question
definition.definition: Assuming, directly or indirectly, the very point that needs to be established, so the conclusion is smuggled into the premises.

source.sectionTitle: God, mind-at-large, and cosmic intelligence
source.currentDescription: If nature is one field of subjectivity, Kastrup concludes that it is omnipresent throughout nature and omniscient concerning the natural states constituting its consciousness.
source.lockedProposition: Because nature is one field of subjectivity, it is conscious of all natural states and omnipresent throughout nature.
source.completeLockedSourceExcerpt: And since it is one field of subjectivity, and that one field of subjectivity is what nature is, then nature is by definition omniscient. It is conscious of everything because it is there consciousness of everything. Right? So it is omniscient. If this field of subjectivity is nature, then it's omnipresent. It's everywhere because it's nature, everywhere.
source.assessmentRationale: Strongest feature: Within Kastrup’s framework, the derivation is economical: a single subject coextensive with nature would be present throughout nature and conscious of the states comprising its experiential field. Principal limitation: “By definition” conceals the contested premise that nature is one unified subject, while “omniscient” ambiguously suggests knowledge extending beyond present natural experience, including possibly unrealized futures. Live burden: Kastrup must defend experiential unity, distinguish present awareness from foreknowledge, and explain how localized dissociation relates to the encompassing field’s knowledge.

presentedReviews.rationale: The unity of nature as one subject is a contested and undefended premise, but that evidential omission alone does not show the conclusion was circularly smuggled into the premise.
The unity of nature as one subject is a crucial contested premise left undefended, but treating a contested premise as given is not by itself circular reasoning or a restatement of the conclusion.

definition.label: Equivocation
definition.definition: Shifting the meaning of a key word or phrase during the argument, making the reasoning seem stronger than it is.

source.sectionTitle: Truth, ways of knowing, humility, and value
source.currentDescription: McGilchrist disputes the dashboard analogy’s epistemic ranking, arguing that richly lived experience is not rendered less real merely because quantitative readouts abstract measurable features.
source.lockedProposition: The dashboard analogy does not establish that lived experience is less real, since experience is richer and the meaning of reality itself remains contested.
source.completeLockedSourceExcerpt: One is you say you use the phrase what the world really is or what it is, but what do we mean when we say what it is? In what sense is my understanding of the world less real than a readout of data showing air pressure, you know, humidity, light and so forth? What is it about my experience, which is infinitely richer than that? That is less theoretical about an aspect of what is, quote, out there than the dashboard?
source.assessmentRationale: Strongest feature: McGilchrist usefully questions an equivocation between reality, measurable description, and fidelity, insisting that qualitative experience cannot be dismissed merely because instrumentation expresses different abstractions. Principal limitation: Experiential richness does not demonstrate closer access to intrinsic reality, and Kastrup need not privilege quantitative readouts over experience; his dashboard analogy concerns functional encoding, not an ontology of measurable data. Live burden: McGilchrist must answer the entropy and fitness mechanisms themselves and explain why qualitative plenitude supports participatory contact rather than richly structured representation.

presentedReviews.rationale: The move explicitly questions a possible conflation of reality, measurement, and fidelity, but it does not itself rely on shifting one key term's meaning to derive its conclusion.

definition.label: Red herring
definition.definition: Diverting attention from the issue under dispute to a related but less relevant point, leaving the original challenge insufficiently answered.

source.sectionTitle: Truth, ways of knowing, humility, and value
source.currentDescription: Love, friendship, art, mathematics, ritual, and religion retain reality and meaning without dial-readable measurement, supporting McGilchrist’s broader qualitative approach to knowledge and value.
source.lockedProposition: Important realities such as love, friendship, art, mathematics, and religion remain meaningful despite not being measurable or readable from a dial.
source.completeLockedSourceExcerpt: But there's enormous number of things. In fact, everything that is important to me that is not measurable. And if you were to measure it, it would have no meaning. Things like love, friendship, sad, poetry, music, painting, ritual, math, religious, or all these things are very real. They're aspects I believe are reality, but they're not measurable and they can't be read off on a dial.
source.assessmentRationale: Strongest feature: McGilchrist marshals varied, familiar examples to show convincingly that human significance, meaningfulness, and experiential reality are not exhausted by quantities available on an instrument’s dial. Principal limitation: Kastrup never commits himself to the claim that only measurable things are real, while mathematics complicates the category and personal importance does not independently prove objective metaphysical value. Live burden: McGilchrist must connect qualitative irreducibility to reliable knowledge of truth, beauty, and goodness and demonstrate that analytic idealism cannot accommodate those same realities.

presentedReviews.rationale: The move rebuts the proposition that only measurable things are real, which Kastrup did not assert, thereby shifting away from his actual claim about perspectival encoding.
presentedReviews.context: all these things are very real. They're aspects I believe are reality, but they're not measurable

presentedReviews.rationale: The catalogue of meaningful but unmeasurable things answers a restriction to measurable reality that Kastrup did not assert, diverting attention from his actual claim about functional perceptual encoding.
presentedReviews.context: Everything that is important to me is not measurable. And if you were to measure it, it would have no meaning.

definition.label: Subjective validation
definition.definition: Treating a claim as especially accurate or meaningful because it feels personally resonant or confirms one's private experience.

source.sectionTitle: Truth, ways of knowing, humility, and value
source.currentDescription: Drawing on psychiatric practice, McGilchrist argues that disciplined imagination can help someone feel into another’s situation, enabling partial interpersonal understanding beyond explicit sensory catalogues.
source.lockedProposition: People can feel their way into another through imagination, as exemplified by psychiatric efforts to understand what it is like to be a patient.
source.completeLockedSourceExcerpt: But for a lot of things you feel your way into them and people may say, well, you do that through your senses, okay, but you do it by an act of imagination. In fact, and having spent many years practicing as a psychiatrist, I spent a lot of time sitting with people and understanding what it must be like to be them.
source.assessmentRationale: Strongest feature: McGilchrist grounds participatory knowing in a concrete professional practice, showing how disciplined imaginative empathy can disclose another person more richly than detached sensory or propositional inventories. Principal limitation: Personal clinical experience cannot verify that empathic understanding accurately reaches another’s intrinsic subjectivity, and imaginative modeling may itself operate representationally rather than bypassing perspective. Live burden: He must offer reliability criteria, acknowledge projection and correction, and explain why successful empathy supports ontological participation instead of sophisticated inference from expression and context.

presentedReviews.rationale: Personal confidence derived from years of psychiatric empathy is used to support imaginative contact with others' inner lives, although that felt understanding cannot itself verify access to their intrinsic subjectivity.
presentedReviews.context: having spent many years practicing as a psychiatrist, I spent a lot of time sitting with people and understanding what it must be like

presentedReviews.rationale: Clinical experience illustrates imaginative empathy, but the speaker does not expressly deem his interpretations accurate merely because they felt personally resonant; the stated defect is missing reliability criteria.

definition.label: Argument from ignorance
definition.definition: Treating a claim as true because it has not been disproved, or false because it has not been proved, rather than supplying positive evidence.

source.sectionTitle: Purpose, suffering, human significance, and culture
source.currentDescription: Because mountains persist longer than organisms and complex lives may shorten, McGilchrist argues that bare endurance cannot exhaust life’s explanation, leaving legitimate room for purpose.
source.lockedProposition: Life cannot be explained merely as persistence because mountains endure for billions of years while more complex lives have become shorter.
source.completeLockedSourceExcerpt: so why is the life at all? We're told it, you know, it's a striving for persistence in being. Maybe if you want to persist in being, it's much better to be inanimate. I mean, a mountain can last for billions of years. We only lasts for short periods. But I'd also mentioned to that over the course of evolution, our lives have got shorter, not longer.
source.assessmentRationale: Strongest feature: The mountain comparison vividly exposes the inadequacy of equating life’s purpose with maximal temporal persistence, since enduring inanimate objects outperform vulnerable organisms on that narrow criterion. Principal limitation: Evolutionary survival concerns differential reproduction rather than the durability of individual entities, the generalized shortening claim needs qualification, and Kastrup did not reduce human purpose to persistence. Live burden: McGilchrist must identify the actual rival explanation, distinguish selection pressure from existential purpose, and move from rejecting survival-only accounts to positively establishing value-directed teleology.

presentedReviews.rationale: Rejecting maximal persistence does not supply positive evidence for teleology, but the move only leaves room for purpose rather than explicitly declaring purpose true because a rival account was disproved.

source.currentDescription: Humans possess heightened capacity to experience ultimate values, McGilchrist concludes, and therefore can freely nourish, magnify, ignore, or vilify those values through their lives.
source.lockedProposition: Mammals, especially humans, have an increasing capacity to experience ultimate values and can reflect, magnify, nourish, ignore, or vilify them.
source.completeLockedSourceExcerpt: mammals, more than any other living creatures, and humans more than other apes and apes more than the rest of the animals, have the capacity to experience these values. The ultimate values, and therefore ought to reflect them and to magnify them by their own lives, by, by, by, by doing something to to nourish them and we can choose to ignore you can choose to vilify them.
source.assessmentRationale: Strongest feature: McGilchrist completes his constructive account by joining evolutionary capacity, free agency, and responsibility: beings able to experience value can actively amplify or diminish its realization. Principal limitation: The hierarchy among animals and humans is asserted without evidence, “ultimate values” remains undefined, and the inference from greater capacity to an obligation to magnify value requires an additional normative bridge. Live burden: He must establish objective value, justify the species comparison, and show that value-realization explains cosmic purpose better than Kastrup’s divine self-discovery.

presentedReviews.rationale: The existence of ultimate values and a hierarchy of access to them are asserted premises needing evidence, but the normative conclusion is not simply repeated in those premises, so exact circularity is not shown.

source.text: The entropy argument asserted that perceptual mirroring would remove an upper bound on internal entropy and make perception fatal without explaining the decisive technical bridge or matching McGilchrist’s qualified contact claim.

presentedReviews.rationale: The blunder says the entropy argument failed to match McGilchrist's qualified contact claim, describing an attack on a stronger mirroring thesis that left the actual position unanswered.

definition.label: Confirmation bias
definition.definition: Seeking, interpreting, or remembering evidence in ways that favor an existing view while discounting contrary information.

source.text: The fitness argument overstated summarized game-theoretic results with the categorical claim that evolution would never optimize veridical perception, overlooking possible correlations between accuracy and adaptive success.

presentedReviews.rationale: Overlooking possible accuracy-fitness correlations makes the argument incomplete and overstated, but the text does not describe selective evidence handling caused by an existing belief or inferred psychological disposition.

definition.label: Scope neglect
definition.definition: Failing to adjust judgment in proportion to the scale, number, or magnitude of what is being discussed.

source.text: The inference from cosmic vastness and complexity to intelligence did not define intelligence or compare non-intelligent sources of order, making structural magnitude carry more argumentative weight than warranted.

presentedReviews.rationale: The blunder says structural magnitude carries excessive argumentative weight, whereas scope neglect requires insufficient adjustment for scale or magnitude; the described error points in the opposite direction.
